parts.latex:
It is given that $A = \dfrac{h}{2}(a + b)$ and $h = 7$, $a = 9$ and $b = 11$.

What is the value of $A$?

solutions.latex:
Substitute into the given formula.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{7}{2}(9 + 11) \\ &= 70 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is A.

parts.latex:
The kinetic energy, $K$ (j) of a particle of mass $M$ (kg), with a velocity of $V$ (m/s) is given by:

$$K=\dfrac{1}{2}MV^2$$

Calculate the value of $K$, if $M=30$ kg and $V=22$ m/s

solutions.latex:
Substitute $M=30$ and $V=22$ into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned} K &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 30\times 22^2 \\ &= 15\times 484 \\ &= 7260 \text{ j} \end{aligned}$$
So the answer is option B.

parts.latex:
The formula $C = \dfrac{5}{9}(F - 32)$ is used to convert temperatures between degrees Fahrenheit ($F$) and degrees Celsius ($C$).

Convert $7^\circ C$ to the equivalent temperature in Fahrenheit.
can_use: Changing the subject of a formula

solutions.latex:
Substitute $C = 7$ into the formula.
$$7 = \dfrac{5}{9}(F-32)$$
Multiply both sides by $\dfrac{9}{5}$.
$$\begin{aligned} F - 32 &= 7 \times \dfrac{9}{5} \\ &= 12.6 \\ F &= 12.6 + 32 \\ &= 44.6 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 7^\circ\text{C} = 44.6^\circ\text{F}$$
criteria: Substitutes $C=7$ and finds $F-32 = 12.6$, or equivalent merit
Substitutes $C=7$ into the formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: If $P=3x+12$ and $x$ is decreased by 3, what will be the corresponding change in $P$?
can_use: Determining the gradient and the y-intercept

solutions.latex:
The coefficient of $x$ is $3$, so decreasing $x$ by $3$ changes $P$ by
$$3\times(-3)=-9$$
$$\therefore\ P\text{ decreases by }9$$
criteria: Makes some progress, or equivalent merit

7403.stem: The distance, $d$, in kilometres that a speed camera can see when placed at a height, $h$, in metres above the ground is given by the formula $d = \sqrt{\dfrac{h}{6.5}}$.

parts.latex: If the camera is placed 4 metres above ground, how far can it see? Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
Rearrange the formula $d = \sqrt{\dfrac{h}{6.5}}$ to make $h$ the subject.
parts.note: Rearranging a formula with a square root is beyond linear and y = ax^2 + c.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $h=4$ into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned} d &= \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{6.5}} \\ &\approx 0.78 \text{ km} \end{aligned}$$
The camera can see about $0.78$ km.

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
Square both sides to remove the square root.
$$d^2=\dfrac{h}{6.5}$$
Multiply both sides by $6.5$.
$$h = 6.5d^2$$
criteria: Squares both sides, or equivalent merit
